info.name: Order Fulfillment System
info.description:
End-to-end test cases for examples/order-system.

SETUP
1. ../boot-infra-dependencies.sh
2. each module's boot-dependencies.sh
3. start the apps with DEMO_MODE=true so nothing advances on its own:
     DEMO_MODE=true java -jar <module>/target/<module>-1.0.0.jar

Folders 01-05 and 08 need DEMO_MODE=true (they step the pipeline by hand).
Folders 06, 07 and 09 work either way.

Kafka propagation is not instant. When running the whole collection, allow a delay between
requests:  newman run order-system.postman_collection.json --delay-request 4000
When clicking through by hand, pause a few seconds between steps - that pause is the demo.

item.name: 01. Happy Path
item.description: The full lifecycle, one step at a time. Requires DEMO_MODE=true so nothing advances on its own.

request.description: The real ingress: an external party publishes the order onto Kafka. The manager consumes it into the order-intake-event flow.
Drains the manager outbox to Kafka. In DEMO_MODE the scheduler does nothing, so this is what moves the order to the steward.
The Kafka ingress does not answer with a fulfillment id (nobody is waiting), so it is read back from the manager and stored for the SoR steps below.

exec: pm.test("order is in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Ticks every SCHEDULED fulfillment. Resumes the graph past checkpoint 1: SCHEDULED -> DISPATCHED.
Drains the steward outbox: sor.dispatch and every fulfillment.status event.
Publishes the 'validated' milestone on its own SoR topic. Each one resumes a workflow that exists only as a Redis key between steps.

exec: pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Publishes the 'preprocessed' milestone on its own SoR topic. Each one resumes a workflow that exists only as a Redis key between steps.

exec: pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Publishes the 'processed' milestone on its own SoR topic. Each one resumes a workflow that exists only as a Redis key between steps.

exec: pm.test("published to the SoR topic", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: Drains the steward outbox: sor.dispatch and every fulfillment.status event.

Publishes the external order-status notification. It is staged in the manager's outbox by the same transaction that concluded the order, so this step has real work to do - it used to be a no-op because the notification was published directly from the flow instead.
The external report, served entirely from the manager's CQRS read model - it never queries the steward.

item.name: 05. Business Rejection (amount = 0)
item.description: An order that fails the graph's own validation never reaches the SoR. The lifecycle stops at REJECTED after two transitions and no sor.dispatch is ever published.

request.description: The real ingress: an external party publishes the order onto Kafka. The manager consumes it into the order-intake-event flow.
Drains the manager outbox to Kafka. In DEMO_MODE the scheduler does nothing, so this is what moves the order to the steward.
The rejection happens inside the STEWARD's graph, so its fulfillment.status event must be relayed before the manager can know about it. Without this step the manager still reports RECEIVED.
Rejected before dispatch.

item.name: 06. Intake Validation (REST)
item.description: The REST ingress answers a bad order with 400 through the flow's exception handler. These run with or without DEMO_MODE.

exec: pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing order_id"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing route"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing payload"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing order_id"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("Missing order_id"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("must start with 'O'"));
pm.test("message names the problem", () => pm.expect(b.message).to.include("must start with 'O'"));

item.name: 07. Kafka Ingress + Dead Letter
item.description: Over Kafka nobody is waiting for an answer, so a malformed order must DEAD-LETTER rather than be silently dropped. That is why the event flow deliberately has no exception handler.

exec: pm.test("found in the read model", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: The mock performs no validation - sending a bad order is the point.

exec: pm.test("the mock publishes it regardless", () => pm.response.to.have.status(202));

request.description: It should be sitting in orders.inbound.dlq instead. Verify with: node node/list-topics.mjs

item.name: 08. Idempotency
item.description: Self-contained: runs a full lifecycle of its own, then replays acknowledgements against the settled fulfillment. Each replay finds its Redis record already consumed, so it becomes a no-op - nothing in the read model may change. Needs DEMO_MODE=true.

item.name: 09. Operations
item.description: The individual admin endpoints, for poking at a running system.

request.description: Uses {{order_id}}, set by any folder that submits an order. With the default it simply reports found:false.

exec: pm.test("answers found true or false", () => pm.expect(b).to.have.property("found"));

item.name: 10. Out-of-Order Milestones
item.description: All three pass but arrive in the wrong order. The milestones are an unordered SET accumulated in the database, so the fulfillment waits at DISPATCHED until the set is complete and then settles - the order of arrival is irrelevant.

request.description: The real ingress: an external party publishes the order onto Kafka. The manager consumes it into the order-intake-event flow.

request.description: Ticks every SCHEDULED fulfillment. Resumes the graph past checkpoint 1: SCHEDULED -> DISPATCHED.
Drains the steward outbox: sor.dispatch and every fulfillment.status event.
Publishes the 'processed' milestone with outcome pass.
Publishes the 'validated' milestone with outcome pass.
Publishes the 'preprocessed' milestone with outcome pass.
Drains the steward outbox: sor.dispatch and every fulfillment.status event.
Arrival order must change neither the state nor the reason.

item.name: 11. Out-of-Order Failure
item.description: The FAILING milestone arrives first. Under the old sequential model the failure was attributed to whichever checkpoint the workflow happened to be waiting at; the reason now names the milestone that actually failed.
